title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 379 (Application of Act to foreign companies)

content.overview: Sections 380 to 386 (both inclusive) and sections 392 and 393 apply to all foreign companies. Where not less than fifty per cent of the paid-up share capital (equity or preference or both) of a foreign company is held, singly or in the aggregate, by one or more citizens of India or by one or more companies or bodies corporate incorporated in India, or by a combination of them, such company shall comply with the provisions of Chapter XXII and such other prescribed provisions with regard to the business carried on by it in India as if it were a company incorporated in India.
content.glance: ss. 380–386, 392 and 393 apply to all foreign companies; ≥50% Indian-held foreign companies must also comply with Chapter XXII (and prescribed provisions) for Indian business as if incorporated in India.
content.study: Section 379 is the gateway provision of Chapter XXII. Subsection (1) applies sections 380 to 386 and sections 392 and 393 to all foreign companies. Subsection (2) imposes a fuller compliance duty on foreign companies that are at least fifty per cent owned by Indian citizens or Indian-incorporated companies or bodies corporate (singly or in aggregate): they must comply with Chapter XXII and such other prescribed provisions in respect of their Indian business as if they were companies incorporated in India.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: ss. 380–386, 392 and 393 apply to all foreign companies; a foreign company with ≥50% Indian-held capital must also comply with Chapter XXII (and prescribed provisions) for its Indian business as if incorporated in India.

provisions.title: Application of Act to foreign companies

examples.title: Illustration — s. 379
examples.body: A company incorporated in Singapore that establishes a place of business in India is subject to ss. 380–386, 392 and 393. If Indian citizens and Indian companies together hold 60% of its paid-up capital, it must also comply with Chapter XXII and prescribed provisions for its Indian business as if it were an Indian company.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 379?
hypotheticals.analysis: It applies the core foreign-company provisions to all foreign companies and imposes fuller Chapter XXII compliance on those that are at least 50% Indian-held.

misconceptions.trap: Treating every foreign company as fully subject to the whole Act as if incorporated in India.
misconceptions.correction: Full as-if-incorporated compliance under s. 379(2) applies only where ≥50% of paid-up capital is Indian-held; otherwise the core provisions in subsection (1) apply.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 379 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm foreign-company status. II. Apply subsection (1) core provisions. III. Check the 50% Indian-holding test for subsection (2).
